answer: Hypothesis (data-grounded): Among the studies in Experimental Economics represented in this dataset (the 18 `ee` studies from the Experimental Economics replication project, which are exactly the same 18 rows flagged `discipline == "Economics"`), 100% were conducted in a lab setting — i.e., none were run online. Every one of the 18 original experiments has `online.o == 0` (in-person/non-online) and every one of the 18 replication experiments has `online.r == 0`, so the proportion of lab-conducted studies is 18/18 = 1.00 (100%) regardless of whether one considers the original side, the replication side, both-sides per study, or all study rows combined (36/36 = 100%). Because all 18 EE studies are non-online on both the original and replication axes and there are no missing values or duplicates in the relevant fields, the result is fully unambiguous: effectively all Experimental Economics studies in the data were conducted in a lab rather than online setting. (Operationalization assumption: "lab setting" ≈ online flag == 0, i.e., not-online/in-person; `subjects`, `experiment_country`, and `us_lab.*` were NOT used as the venue indicator. For context, 17/18 original experiments and 18/18 replications used student subject pools, with one original (ee.4) using community subjects, and all still flagged non-online.)

payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927x57). 2) Defined Experimental Economics studies as project=='ee' (18 rows) and verified this is identical to discipline=='Economics' (same 18 ids). 3) Operationalized 'lab setting' as online flag == 0 (in-person/not-online); excluded subjects/experiment_country/us_lab.* from the venue definition. 4) Computed lab proportion on the original side (online.o==0: 18/18=1.00), the replication side (online.r==0: 18/18=1.00), the pair-both-lab definition (o==0 and r==0: 18/18=1.00), and all rows combined (36/36=1.00). 5) Confirmed zero missing values in the EE rows and no duplicates (each ee id appears exactly once; global duplicated-ids come from per-lab rows of other projects and do not touch EE). 6) Wrote results to analysis/ee_lab_setting_summary.csv.
payload.hypothesis: 100% of Experimental Economics studies in the dataset were conducted in a lab setting (not online): all 18 originals (online.o==0) and all 18 replications (online.r==0) were run in-person, so the lab proportion is 18/18 = 1.00 on every side.
